thread.title: ‘Google is at Apple’s mercy’ — the trouble in Alphabet’s earnings - MarketWatch

author: Victor Reklaitis
title: ‘Google is at Apple’s mercy’ — the trouble in Alphabet’s earnings - MarketWatch
text:
Yes, the company’s name is Alphabet GOOG, -0.19% GOOGL, -0.05% these days, but it might as well be mud, if you go by what some bears are saying.
They are pouncing following the search king’s weaker-than-expected earnings ( $9.70 for adjusted EPS vs. forecasts for around $10 ).
The miss contrasts with the beats by Apple AAPL, +0.21% and Amazon AMZN, -4.20% — and maybe by this morning’s jobs report, where 190K will be the headline number to top.
One longtime worry for investors is that as people switch away from PCs to smartphones, Google has become more dependent on rivals like Apple to serve up its ads. Perhaps such fears have been confirmed, as Alphabet’s traffic acquisition costs, or TAC, came in above forecasts.
“Google is at Apple’s mercy for search on iPhones, and that hurts because search has moved to mobile devices,” says University of Michigan business school professor Erik Gordon for our call of the day .
This “increases its cost to acquire the revenue,” Gordon tells the FT , which also flags the CFO’s hints about another TAC attack in the current quarter.
Alphabet remains a gorilla that is capable of taking many bananas from other members of tech’s half trillion dollar club . And the stock had roared going into last night’s earnings report, gaining 12% for the year as of yesterday’s close, so don’t cry too much over its premarket drop of 3% or so.
Check out: Google sold at least $2.7 billion worth of hardware during the holidays
At the same time, Morgan Stanley analysts have cut their Alphabet price target to $1,200 from $1,215, as they note “margin-dilutive investments” and a slowdown in YouTube’s growth. But they also backed their overweight rating, and FactSet indicates that 84% of analyst teams covering the stock say buy it.

And see: Google’s cloud unit is a $1 billion business, execs say
Key market gauges Futures for the Dow YMH8, -0.93% , S&P 500 ESH8, -0.74% and Nasdaq-100 NQH8, -0.51% are slumping, putting the blue-chip gauge on track for a drop of more than 200 points. The Dow DJIA, +0.14% , S&P SPX, -0.06% and Nasdaq Composite COMP, -0.35% are all set for weekly drops, with rising bond yields getting much of the blame. The 10-year Treasury yield TMUBMUSD10Y, +1.03% has topped 2.80% and was recently at 2.79%.
Europe SXXP, -1.00% is a sea of red, after Asia mostly closed lower . Oil CLH8, -0.09% and gold GCG8, -0.45% are little changed, while the dollar index DXY, +0.49% is edging up.
See the Market Snapshot column for the latest action.
The chart BAML This BAML gauge says sell. A contrarian sell signal for stocks and other risk assets just got triggered, according to the chart above from Bank of America Merrill Lynch strategists.
BAML’s Bull & Bear Indicator has surged to 8.6 from 7.9, spurred by factors such as record inflows into stocks and bullish bets by hedge funds.
The bank’s strategists note that their clients would rather just shift around trades (“play rotation”) rather than position for a big reversal, with some saying, “We only just got bullish!”
The buzz Daily Shot “Sometimes technical analysis just works.” At least Alphabet shareholders aren’t faring as badly as bitcoin hodlers , as the No. 1 cryptocurrency BTCUSD, -7.50% was recently down about 10% and has traded below $8,000, according to CoinDesk data . The Daily Shot newsletter, which earlier this week noted that bitcoin had undercut a key trend line, is saying “sometimes technical analysis just works.”
Cryptocurrencies wiped out $100 billion in value in about 24 hours , and two economists say a single bitcoin isn’t worth $0 — it’s more like $20 .
Beyond the earnings reports from the three tech titans, Visa V, +1.20% , GoPro GPRO, +0.55% , Merck MRK, +1.03% , Estee Lauder EL, -0.30% and Deutsche Bank DB, +1.69% have posted results.
See: Downgraded Apple faces ‘saturated market’ for iPhones — analysts react to earnings
And see: Bezos’ fortune tops $120 billion as Amazon’s stock soars
There are fresh signs that CBS CBS, +2.29% and Viacom VIAB, -0.63% might merge , while Guess GES, -17.75% is under pressure after Kate Upton alleged harassment by the apparel seller’s co-founder.
On the political front, President Trump is expected to OK the release of a classified memo that allegedly shows improper surveillance. Former FBI boss James Comey is tweeting out support for the agency, saying “ weasels and liars ” never win in the long run, while fake news pioneer The Onion reports the memo “could undermine faith in massive, unaccountable government secret agencies.”
Sony SNE, +2.52% has a new CEO .
Also outside the USA: “Fidelito” Castro reportedly killed himself , and a van in Shanghai plowed into pedestrians, injuring 18, with authorities saying it was an accident , not terrorism.
The stat Have you heard the Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow model is estimating eye-popping 5.4% growth for U.S. Q1 GDP?
